answer: Sybil farms mint keys cheaper than service drops. Bind each payout address to one utility meter: a photo of the serial on its marble service plaque and a 36 POA hold. A shared serial collapses both keys. Each epoch the verifier commands a brief zephyr of load, 30 seconds at 200 W, and the meter signs a cipher of the epoch seed plus that pulse trace with its sealed probe key. Silence or a collision burns the hold. Assumed costs: $90 to open a drop and $20 a month. 140 fakes need 140 drops: $12,600 to start, $2,800 monthly, and 5,040 POA locked, because one probe cannot attest two serials.
